findings.title: The atmosphere canvas is as tall as the whole document, so the WebGPU aurora fails to start on long pages (and on retina screens); the field goes dead or flat
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/color-picker/App.vue:17-18 (canvas `absolute inset-0 w-full h-full` inside .app-layout) + demo/styles/shell.css:78-86 (.app-layout `min-block-size: 100svh`, grows with content)
findings.where: /#/ and /#/palettes at 390 (both themes); /#/ at 1440 dark (About pane unclipped, OA-21)
findings.frame: 390-light-rest-home.png (flat magenta, dead field; boot 1400→4000 ms frame-diff 0.0); 390-dark-rest-home.png; report.json → 390-light/390-dark .routes['/'].canvas {bufW:390, bufH:8687}, 1440-dark .routes['/'].canvas {bufH:7558}
findings.observed:
The canvas grows to the document's scroll height: 390x8687 on /#/ at 390 and 1440x7558 on /#/ at 1440 dark. The WebGPU swapchain texture limit is 8192.
- Console: 'Texture size ([Extent3D width:390, height:8687]) exceeded maximum texture size (8192)' followed by '[aurora] init failed: GPUValidationError'.
- 390-light: the canvas never gets `atmosphere-canvas--arrived` and the ground is a static flat slab.
- 390-dark: 10,820 init-failed warnings in about 90 s (a retry storm).
- 1440 dark at DPR 2 (the owner's 2846x1650 retina surface) would need a 15116-px texture, so it fails the same way.
findings.expected: A full-bleed field sized to the viewport; page content scrolls over it. glass Aurora README §Runtime contract (:30-52): the substrate owns 'backing-store sizing and DPR policy' and 'tab, offscreen … parking'. It is not meant to be a document-sized buffer.
findings.fix: Make the field viewport-fixed: `position: fixed; inset: 0; block-size: 100lvh` (or mount glass <Aurora class="fixed inset-0">) instead of absolute on the growing grid. The backing store is then bounded by the viewport × DPR on every route, however long the scroll.

findings.title: Glass aurora substrate does not keep its backing store within the GPU texture limit, and retries init every frame after a validation error
findings.owner: GLASS — aurora useAurora/createGpuSubstrate (installed 7.0.0 dist/aurora.js dprPolicy ≈:2355; src/components/aurora/composables/runtime.ts:299-318 onInitError path). Canon: aurora/README.md:30-52 'backing-store sizing and DPR policy … engine recovery', and 'Setup and pipeline failures are reported rather than disguised'.
findings.where: any route where the canvas is taller than 8192 device px
findings.frame: report.json → 390-dark.console: 10,820× '[aurora] init failed: [object GPUValidationError]' + 100× 'Could not create the swapchain texture' / '[Invalid CommandBuffer from CommandEncoder "[Aurora] frame"]', then 'WebGPU: too many warnings'
findings.observed: The substrate sizes the swapchain to canvas CSS × DPR with no clamp to device.limits.maxTextureDimension2D. After the validation error it keeps encoding '[Aurora] frame' and re-reporting init failure every frame. It neither drops to its WebGL2 path nor settles on one reported failure.
findings.expected: Clamp the backing store to maxTextureDimension2D (scale DPR down). After a setup failure: report once, set rendererStatus to failed, and fall to the WebGL2 or static CSS product mode. Never loop.
findings.fix: Route to the glass-ui session (O-56 G-4 follow-up with this measurement). Clamp in the shared lifecycle's resize policy, and add a one-shot failure latch that switches to the CSS-gradient mode. No consumer copy.

findings.title: No fallback when the aurora fails: the canvas stays transparent and the ground drops to the tiling body gradient
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:195-199 (`onInitError: (err) => console.warn(...)` only) + App.vue:20-22 (`auroraCssGradient` is bound only when renderMode resolves to 'css')
findings.observed: On a GPU failure at runtime (as opposed to a device-tier 'css' pick) nothing switches to the palette's CSS gradient. The field disappears and the phone ground reads as one flat saturated slab, rgb(200,70,215) in light.
findings.expected: The 'one material from t0' contract that useAtmosphereBoot and overture.css:40-56 describe: the same derived palette paints through the CSS placeholder whenever the GPU field is absent.
findings.fix: In onInitError, and on a rendererStatus of 'failed', set the CSS-placeholder path: paletteToCssGradient(resolvedPalette) onto the canvas background, and mark the canvas arrived.

findings.title: The body ground gradient repeats every viewport height and restarts at its darkest stop below the fold, leaving a near-black band at the end of the document in dark
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/styles/foundation.css:656-663 (body `background-image: linear-gradient(135deg, --saved-bg-0..3)` with no size, repeat or attachment)
findings.where: /#/, /#/palettes, /#/gradient at 390 (scrolled to the end); any page where the document is taller than the canvas
findings.observed: Below the canvas (the document is 1214 px tall, the layout 1208) the page shows rgb(39,0,27)→rgb(58,0,31). That is --saved-bg-0 restarting at x≈0, a hard seam of near-black plum under the last card. It is one reproducible source of the owner's 'background goes black'.
findings.expected: One continuous ground with no seam and no tile restart (the W2-2 'one material' ground).
findings.fix: `background-attachment: fixed` plus no-repeat on the body ground, or paint the ground on the same viewport-fixed field layer as the canvas. Also find and remove the 5–6 px of scroll beyond .app-layout.

findings.title: The dark-theme field is near-black by construction: the dark lightness band makes the ground read as black, not as a coloured atmosphere (OA-18)
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:188-193 (fieldAtoms injects `lightnessScheme: "dark"` → band L 0.18–0.42 per its own comment :172-176). GLASS if the default band is the fix: deriveAurora dark-scheme band.

findings.title: View switch: the vacated inspector slot shows an over-saturated, plate-shaped slab for about 1 s while the next pane slides in from off-screen, then the scene jumps 48 px
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/color-picker/App.vue pane regions (pane-wrapper--stage/--inspector) + demo/styles/animations.css:246-292 (the pane vj-enter overrides); the jump comes from OA-21's unclipped About pane
findings.observed:
1440 dark, / → /palettes (chunk already warm):
- The inspector rect (x 730–1240) shows a bright field-coloured slab while the old About pane leaves to the right and the new pane arrives from x≈1300.
- elementFromPoint in the slot is a bare `div.pane-wrapper`: transparent, no backdrop-filter.
- The main thread did not answer between +111 ms and +1103 ms.
- The card top moves from 112 to 160 px as the tall About pane leaves.
On the other switches, the stage is empty for a frame while the leaving card is still on screen.
findings.expected: One short, bounded enter/leave per region on glass motion tokens (X.W12.b). No empty or flat-filled slot, no layout jump, no long task during the swap.
findings.fix: Enter each incoming pane in its own slot (short translate, not an off-screen slide) so the slot is never empty. Identify the layer painting the slab; it cannot be hit-tested, so likely the leaving plate's backdrop or pseudo layer left in place. Break up the ~1 s long task on switch. Clip About to the stage's height (X.W12.c) so the grid does not re-centre.

findings.title: The Picker stage replays its entrance on views where it persists, and one card has two animation owners on transform
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/color-picker/App.vue region render/keying; demo/color-picker/composables/boot/overture.css (plate-land) vs animations.css vj-enter transform transition
findings.observed:
On / → /palettes the persisting picker runs `field-paint-in` (420 ms) on div.spectrum-picker, plus 4× `stagger-child-in` (300 ms) on the channel-rail items and 4× on the channel strips. It is re-mounted and re-animated even though the pane did not change.
On /atmosphere → /: `div.glass-resting.card` has `T:transform@440ms` at +50 ms, then `A:plate-land@440ms` at +654 ms. That is a transition and a keyframe animation both owning transform (the OA-25 'double animated').
findings.expected: A pane shared by both views stays still. Each element has one motion owner per property (X.W12.b gate).
findings.fix: Key the stage region by pane id, not by view, so a shared pane does not re-mount. Take the card enter transform out of either the vj-enter transition or plate-land.

findings.title: The per-view accent stays locked to admin gold after visiting /atmosphere or /blob, even when logged out; the 9-view 40° hue steps disappear
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/shell/dock/composables/useDockAdminMode.ts:55-59 (the watch only ever sets `isAdminMode = true`; nothing sets it back when the view is a user view)
findings.where: every user view after one visit to /#/atmosphere or /#/blob
findings.frame: probe-accent-seq2.json (/atmosphere → / → /gradient → /mix: each svg has `gold-shimmer-icon`, colour oklch(0.751 0.147 84.2), while `--accent-view` on the trigger is per-view); probe-accent-*.png; montage-1440-light-accent-9views.png and montage-1440-dark-accent-9views.png (all 9 icons gold); crop-1440-light-viewicon-gradient-x4.png
findings.observed: After one admin-class view the dock icon and ring are gold on every view. The painted icon pixel is rgb(218,165,31) on home, palettes, gradient and mix. The dock still shows 'Login', so the user is not authenticated. The schema's accentHueShift 280/320 for atmosphere and blob never shows either, because those views always render gold.
findings.expected: viewSchema.ts:129-140: 'the nine … hue rotation', and 'admin identity is the gold accent' applies only in admin mode. Leaving admin views should restore the per-view accent.
findings.fix: Derive isAdminMode (computed from currentView ∈ adminViews AND isAdminAuthenticated) instead of a one-way latched ref. Decide whether atmosphere and blob are user views (with a hue) or admin views (gold), not both.

findings.title: The hand-mounted <canvas> + useAurora re-implements glass <Aurora> and loses its contracts (sizing, fallback, status)
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/color-picker/App.vue:17-25 (raw <canvas>) + demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:195-199 (useAurora on it)
findings.observed: The field is a consumer canvas driven by the lower-level useAurora. Sizing (findings 1 and 2) and failure fallback (finding 3) are the consumer's job and both are broken.
findings.expected: glass aurora/README.md:1-28: use the <Aurora :config> primitive, which owns product mode, sizing, parking and fallback.
findings.fix: Mount glass <Aurora class="fixed inset-0" :config :on-init-error>, keeping the `data-glass-field-canvas` stamp (ask glass to forward it if needed). Keep only the palette and atoms derivation in the consumer.

findings.title: Error state in a scene region: fallback text sits directly on the field (no glass plate) with a square browser-default blue focus outline
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:24-26 (tabindex=-1 plate) + :102 (programmatic focus)
findings.frame: 1440-light-rest-home.png (x 728–1242 blue square-cornered outline; heading, mono error text and 'Try again' on the bare field)

The raw module URL is shown in mono. (Trigger here: a Vite 504 Outdated Optimize Dep; the same state happens in production after a deploy.)

findings.title: In dark, all nine per-view accents collapse to near-white, so the hue step is invisible
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useViewAccents.ts (the contrast solve lands at L≈0.958)

findings.title: One navigation runs on three different clocks (ground 200 ms, accent sweep 550 ms, pane plate 440 ms)
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/styles/foundation.css:676-681 (ground 200 ms); demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:159-161 (`--accent-view` over --duration-panel, measured 550 ms); overture.css:16 (plate-land 440 ms)

confirm.page: value.js · app-ground-atmosphere. Fresh confirm seat, read-only. Re-checked on 2026-09-23 against value.js 9b8fb106 (5 dirty) and glass-ui 6433284a (3 dirty, all untracked docs/.vite-temp), installed glass 7.0.0. Evidence: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/X/audit/ui-evidence/value/app-ground-atmosphere/ (report.json, probe-slab.json, probe-accent-seq2.json, and the frames named below). I opened the frames and re-read the source citations against the current trees. No new captures were taken. Tally: 8 CONFIRMED, 4 AMENDED, 0 REFUTED.

verdicts.title: 1 · The atmosphere canvas is as tall as the whole document, so the WebGPU aurora fails on long pages
verdicts.why: The mechanism holds. App.vue:17 is still `absolute inset-0 w-full h-full` inside .app-layout, and shell.css:78-86 is `min-block-size:100svh` with nothing capping it. report.json has bufH 8687 on / at 390 in both themes, and the console has 'Texture size ([Extent3D width:390, height:8687]) exceeded maximum texture size'. Two corrections. (a) 1440-dark / measured bufH 7558 at DPR 1, which is under 8192. That run had no init failure, so the 'where' entry '/#/ at 1440 dark' is only a projection for retina. (b) The retina figure is wrong. Installed glass 7.0.0 clamps aurora DPR to 1.5 (dist color.wgsl-Ct5o9dpf.js `var a = 1.5`, fed as aurora.js:2355 dprPolicy), so retina needs 7558×1.5 ≈ 11337 px, not 15116. That still fails. Also, 1440-light / was only 900 px tall because About had been replaced by the error boundary. The canvas height follows the unclipped About pane (OA-21), so the tall canvas and the About clip are one root cause.

verdicts.title: 2 · The glass aurora substrate has no texture-limit clamp and retries init every frame (GLASS)
verdicts.why: Glass owns this, and the call is correct. aurora/README.md:34-42 says the shared lifecycle owns 'backing-store sizing and DPR policy' and 'engine recovery'. A grep for `maxTextureDimension` finds nothing in glass src or in the installed dist. useWebGPUCanvas.ts:20-22 sizes the backing store to clientWidth × dpr and says 'the swap chain auto-resizes … no configure needed on resize'. The storm in 390-dark is measured: 10,820 init-failed warnings plus 100× 'Could not create the swapchain texture' and 'Invalid CommandBuffer "[Aurora] frame"'. Amendment to the citation: runtime.ts:299-318 is the image-coordinator and unavailable-report path, not the per-frame error path. The flood comes from the uncapturederror listener in useWebGPUCanvas.ts:234-264, which reaches onInitError after arm. Also, 390-light logged only 2 failures because there the size was over the limit at setup, so the fatal-release path ran. The storm happens only when the canvas grows past 8192 after arm. The glass fix needs to cover both paths.

verdicts.title: 3 · No fallback when the aurora fails; the canvas stays transparent and the ground goes flat
verdicts.why: useAtmosphere.ts:198 is `onInitError: (err) => console.warn(...)` only. :235-239 sets auroraCssGradient only when `auroraRenderMode === 'css'`, which is decided up front, so a runtime failure never switches to the CSS gradient. 390-light-rest-home.png is one flat magenta field. report.json shows bgImage 'none' and no arrived class on any 390-light route, including /palettes at bufH 1208, which is under the limit. Once init fails, the field never re-arms after navigating to a shorter page, which makes the case stronger. Secondary: in 390-dark the canvas carries `atmosphere-canvas--arrived` even though every frame fails. That class comes from overture.b2 (App.vue:19), not from renderer status, so 'arrived' does not tell you whether the field is actually painting.

verdicts.title: 4 · The body ground gradient leaves a near-black seam at the end of the document
verdicts.why: The seam is real. crop-390-dark-palettes-scrollend-bottom-x4.png shows a hard dark-plum band under the last card. report 390-dark /palettes has docScrollH 1214 against layout h 1208, and the scroll-end sample at (195,838) is rgb(51,0,30) at lum 0.051. The owner site foundation.css:656-663 is correct: body has a gradient with no attachment, size or repeat set. What is not proven is 'repeats every viewport height / restarts at its darkest stop'. No frame separates a tile restart from where the root background's positioning area starts. Restate as: the ground below .app-layout is the body gradient, not the field, and it is darkest there. The fix (paint the ground on the viewport-fixed field layer, or use background-attachment:fixed, and remove the 6 px of overflow past .app-layout) stands.

verdicts.title: 5 · The dark-theme field is near-black by construction (OA-18)
verdicts.why: The band is real. useAtmosphere.ts:188-193 injects `lightnessScheme:'dark'`, and its own comment (:181-184) measures L 0.18-0.42. But 1440-dark-rest-home.png does not read as black. It is a hued plum-to-crimson atmosphere, dark on the left third and clearly coloured on the right. The audit's own idle samples found no black at all. Downgrade to MEDIUM ('dark and muddy on the left third, not black'). The black the owner sees reproduces only at the seam (finding 4) and in the failed-field paths (findings 1-3). Lifting the band is a tuning choice, not a defect fix. The owner call (CONSUMER through the atoms door) is correct.

verdicts.title: 6 · View switch shows a saturated, plate-shaped slab in the vacated inspector slot, then the scene jumps
verdicts.why: probe-slab-dark-home-to-palettes-1.png shows a solid crimson slab with rounded top corners at x≈730-1240 while About slides off to the right, and there is no content in the slot. probe-slab.json shows elementFromPoint at +64, +111 and +1103 ms landing on a transparent div.pane-wrapper with no backdrop-filter. The canvas is pointer-events-none, so the painting layer cannot be hit-tested, as the audit says. Owner is CONSUMER; nothing points at glass.

verdicts.title: 7 · The Picker stage replays its entrance on views where it persists, and one card has two animation owners on transform
verdicts.why: report.json 1440-light switches[0] (/ → /palettes) at +100 ms: div.spectrum-picker has A:field-paint-in@420ms, plus 4× stagger-child-in on the channel-rail items and 4× on the channel strips. 1440-dark switches[3] (/atmosphere → /) shows glass-resting.card with 'T:transform@440ms' in one census and 'T:transform@440ms','A:plate-land@440ms' on the same row in the next, so two owners run on transform.

verdicts.title: 8 · The per-view accent stays latched to admin gold after visiting /atmosphere or /blob
verdicts.why: useDockAdminMode.ts:55-59 only ever sets isAdminMode = true. The only reset is the logout watch at :62-64, which never fires for a user who never authenticated. probe-accent-seq2.json shows gold-shimmer-icon and svgColor oklch(0.751 0.147 84.2) on /, /gradient and /mix while trigAccent takes the per-view hue (9.8°, 249.8°, 169.8°), and adminText still includes 'Login'. viewSchema.ts:129-140 says admin views stay at 0° because gold is the admin identity. So the 280/320 accentHueShift the audit cites for atmosphere and blob cannot be seen by construction. That part is a schema contradiction, not a separate bug.

verdicts.title: 9 · The hand-mounted <canvas> + useAurora re-implements glass <Aurora> and loses its contracts
verdicts.why: App.vue:17-25 uses a raw canvas, and useAtmosphere.ts:195-200 calls useAurora directly. glass Aurora.vue:128-143 owns the onInitError routing and product mode that the consumer is missing here. The owner call is correct: CONSUMER, plus asking glass to forward the data-glass-field-canvas stamp if needed. Adopting <Aurora> alone does not fix the texture clamp (finding 2 is still glass's).

verdicts.title: 10 · Error state: fallback sits on the bare field with a square blue focus outline
verdicts.why: 1440-light-rest-home.png shows a 2 px blue square-cornered outline at x 728-1242, a heading, a raw @fs module URL in mono, and 'Try again' directly on the field. ErrorBoundary.vue:20-28 renders the glass EmptyState variant='error' with tabindex=-1 and no card wrapper, and :102 calls plateRef.focus() in nextTick. The file has no outline rule. The owner stays CONSUMER: EmptyState is plate-less by design, so the consumer has to supply the Card. The frame has been cited as 1440-light-rest-home.png throughout; note that this is also the reason 1440-light's canvas is only 900 px tall.

verdicts.title: 11 · In dark, all nine per-view accents collapse to near-white
verdicts.why: The data holds: 390-dark /palettes has accentView oklch(0.958 0.023 49.8). The attribution is off. The input axis itself, accentLive, is already oklch(95.8% 0.021 9.8°) in dark (report tokens.accentLive), so useViewAccents rotates an axis that is already near-white and low in chroma. Its C-floor lifts only some hues (/extract C 0.08). The owner site is the dark derivation of --accent-live, upstream of useViewAccents, plus the C-floor, which should apply to every view and not only to hues that fall out of gamut.

verdicts.title: 12 · One navigation runs on three different clocks
verdicts.why: The three clocks are confirmed: foundation.css:676-681 is 200 ms, the census shows --accent-view@550ms, and plate-land is 440ms. The audit undercounts. The same /atmosphere → / census also shows A:blob-emerge@500ms and canvas.goo-blob-canvas A:substrate-reveal-bloom@1100ms, which make five clocks with the longest at 1100 ms. Several pane-header animations also report '@NaNms' in the census (pane-header-veil, pane-title-shrink, pane-desc-shrink): the tool could not read their durations, and that is unverified.

findings.owner: GLASS — SelectContent (glass-ui src/components/select/SelectContent.vue:84 has min-w only, no max-width tied to the available width; collisionPadding 16 at :56 cannot shift a box wider than the viewport). Contributing: CONSUMER demo/color-session/ColorSpaceSelector.vue:379 (the caption max-width is a character budget, so the specimen row sets the width)

findings.observed: The listbox is 413px wide from x=16, so its right edge is at 429 on a 390 viewport. The right border, the selected-row card edge and the ends of long specimen strings go off-screen.
findings.expected: A popover fits the viewport minus the 16px gutter (DESIGN.md: --radius-card popover role :387; page contract of no horizontal overflow and a 16px gutter).
findings.fix: glass: SelectContent gets max-w-(--reka-select-content-available-width), clamped to 100vw minus 2x the collision padding. consumer: let the specimen caption truncate below its character budget in narrow bands, or wrap the caption under the name.

findings.title: Header condense is inverted: it fires at 1440 over the sliders and never at 390
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/picker/composables/useHeaderCondense.ts:65-73 (resolveScrollRoot returns null at lg because the card's lg:overflow-visible beats overflow-x-hidden, so the viewport is the root), :93 (the sufficiency gate is skipped when scrollRoot is null); demo/picker/header.css:24-27 (position: sticky); demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:9 (card overflow classes)
findings.observed: At 1440, page scroll condenses the header, and the sticky strip rides down over the card's own content. The display-1 readout sits on top of the L slider row, with the L track and the '92.0%' meter showing through under the numerals. The veil only covers the title band and paints a muddy grey slab (the backdrop-blurred spectrum) with a hard lower edge. At 390, where this state was built for, condensed=false: the card is the observed root but never overflows (scrollHeight 602 = clientHeight 602), so the header just scrolls away.
findings.expected: Per the composable's own contract (ColorPicker.vue:136-145): condense only where the picker actually scrolls (mobile), stay expanded at desktop, and the veil covers the whole strip (header.css:47-55 'rows never ghost-through').
findings.fix: Resolve the scroll root to the element that actually scrolls (the app scroll host at <lg), and never condense when the root is the viewport and the card fits. Size the veil to the condensed strip, including the readout, or cap the sticky range inside the card.

findings.title: Readout line-lock leaves about 61px of dead air between the title and the numbers at 1440, and orphans '20.0' onto a second line at 390
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/readoutReservation.ts:192-208 (readoutLineCount returns 2 for Lab from a static capacity constant); ColorComponentDisplay.vue style: min-height calc(var(--readout-lines)*1.12em) plus align-content: flex-end

verdicts.title: Space-select popover overflows the viewport at 390
verdicts.why: 390-dark-08 shows the listbox's right border and the selected 'Lab' row cut off at the viewport edge. SelectContent.vue:84 has only min-w-(--overlay-min-width) and :106 min-w-(--reka-select-trigger-width), with no max-w anywhere, and collisionPadding 16 (:56) cannot shrink the box. The GLASS-primary / CONSUMER-contributing split is correct.

verdicts.title: Header condense is inverted (fires at 1440, never at 390)
verdicts.why: 1440-light-11-condense.json reports condensed=true with sh=ch=683, and the frame shows the tuple over the L row with the veil only on the title band (a grey slab with a hard lower edge). 390-light-11-condense.json reports condensed=false with sh=ch=602, and the header has scrolled away. useHeaderCondense.ts resolveScrollRoot returns null for the viewport fallback, and the sufficiency gate is inside `if (scrollRoot && head)`, so with a null root the header condenses unconditionally. The CONSUMER owner call is correct.

verdicts.title: ConsoleRail is a stadium pill around a vertical column
verdicts.why: ConsoleRail.vue:228 sets border-radius: var(--radius-pill). DESIGN.md's role table assigns --radius-strip (0.75rem, 12px) to a 'Bounded column-stack segmented track (vertical)' and keeps stadium for horizontal tabs and controls. Every frame shows the capsule. The CONSUMER plus glass variant routing is correct, and this is the owner's 'too rounded' instance.

verdicts.title: Readout line-lock dead band at 1440 / orphaned '20.0' at 390
verdicts.why: 1440-light-02 shows about a 1-line empty band between 'Lab' and the tuple, and 390-light-01 has '20.0' alone on line 2. readoutLineCount (readoutReservation.ts:192-208) greedy-packs against the static READOUT_LINE_CAPACITY_CH, not the measured width. CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: Channel values shown twice; About repeats the space selector
verdicts.why: 1440-dark-01 shows the hero tuple 92.0/88.8/20.0 and the meters 92.0%/88.8/20.0/82.7%, and the About title carries a second 'Lab ⌄' trigger. Both are also visible at 390 (390-light-11 About title). CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: Nested plates not concentric; card publishes --radius-inset 0
verdicts.why: In glass-ui, --radius-inset is published only by overlay-plate.css:65/116. The Card component source has no --radius-inset (grep of src/components/card is empty), so the DESIGN.md relay default of 0px holds and a nested plate gets ctx−0 = 16 instead of max(4, 16−21). The GLASS owner half (Card should publish its pad) is valid alongside the consumer overrides (rounded-panel, --radius-xl).

verdicts.title: Readout value edit has no commit/cancel
verdicts.why: The behaviour is confirmed: 1440-light-11 still shows the '88.8' edit box persisting after the probe flow, and Escape handling is gated on isEditing (editTarget !== null). The line refs have drifted: the Escape branch is now at ColorPicker.vue:258-259 (isEditing at :281), not :193-205. Dock.vue:88-89 is still correct: mobileEditActive = !isDesktop && !!editTarget, where editTarget is a destructured prop and not a ref, so it is not always-truthy.

verdicts.title: Out-of-gamut values shown raw with no visible marker
verdicts.why: 390-dark-08 shows 'hsl(346deg -1295% 103.7% …)', 'rgb(385.3 …)', 'hwb(… -51.1% …)' and 'hsv · … · 1.511' with no glyph. The spectrum handle pins at the top edge in 1440-light-02 and 390-light-01 with no gamut cue. CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: Space-select specimens heavy and grammar-inconsistent
verdicts.why: 390-dark-08: rows are two-line cards with an about 36px italic display name, about 4 rows show per scroll port, HSV uses the dotted pseudo-syntax next to CSS functions, and the selected row is a nested bordered card. CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: Dark theme card reads opaque brown on red ground
verdicts.why: 1440-dark-01 and 390-dark-08 show a flat brown slab and a darker brown console plate. DESIGN.md:17 says 'NEVER gray/dark/opaque, both modes'. The split owner call (glass dark resting tier plus the consumer ground) is right. The page-wide scope (About card, dock) makes it a systemic dark-arm issue more than a picker one.

verdicts.title: HeroBlob ornament: matte ball in light, blown-out orb in dark; costs header space
verdicts.why: 1440-light-02 shows a blurred matte pink ball, while 1440-dark-01 and 390-dark-08 show a featureless white orb. At 390 it sits beside a title row that is reserved but mostly empty. Owner decision; the routing is right.

verdicts.title: 390 slider thumbs 12x44 overhang the track; grey square halo

verdicts.why: In 390-light-09 the 'O' of OKLCh touches the ring's left inner edge. :327-328 uses box-shadow var(--focus-ring-shadow) with border-radius var(--radius-md). --radius-md is not a role token in the DESIGN.md:383-395 table.

verdicts.title: HSV and Kelvin captions use a different format from the other 16 rows

verdicts.title: Opening the list collapses the dock to a dot at 1440 but not at 390
verdicts.why: The behavior is confirmed. With the list closed, the dock is a full pill in 1440-light-01 and p2-1440-dark-11. With it open, the dock is a dot in 1440-light-05, 1440-dark-06 and p2-1440-dark-12. At 390 it stays a pill in 390-light-05. The owner cite is wrong, though. useDockParticipation (glass _shared/overlay/participation.ts:104-125) only stamps and holds overlays that are inside a dock context (`dock?.id`). The picker's Select is not dock-owned, so `dock.portalAttrs` is empty and does nothing here. The collapse is the dock's own idle / outside-interaction collapse, which fires in the 1440 full-dock register but not in the 390 compact register. Re-route to GLASS dock collapse policy (and value.js's dock config), not overlay participation. It is a dock-cohesion item (COHESION §0ao dock pills) more than a selector defect.

findings.title: Opening the color input collapses the dock to the swatch orb and leaves the 'Enter a color' popover floating on its own
findings.owner: GLASS (GlassDock collapse state machine — dock/README.md 'Interaction contracts': portaled popovers keep the dock open through the typed dock context; collapse must hold while a hosted popover is open or a layer is morphing) + CONSUMER (demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:136-149 fit-content layer swap resizes the dock under the pointer)
findings.state: input mode, just opened (reproduced in 3 of 4 runs at 1440-light; the 4th run did not collapse)
findings.observed: The pointer rests where the user clicked 'Open color input'. Within 0.8 s the dock morphs to fit the 325px field, then collapses to the 56px swatch orb. Meanwhile the hover popover ('Enter a color / lab(...) / LAB l 92%... / outside srgb gamut') opens anyway and hangs beside the orb, pointing at nothing. Reaching the field takes another click to re-expand.
findings.expected: Entering the input arm is an explicit mode: the dock stays expanded while the arm is open, focus-within holds, or a hosted popover is open. The field receives focus. No popover opens that the user did not ask for.
findings.fix: Glass: add the open-popover and focus-within collapse hold to the GlassDock state machine, and never start the collapse timer from a pointerleave caused by the dock's own morph. Consumer: while toolbarMode !== 'actions', seat the arm as an always-expanded hold and focus() the field on open (the watch at ColorInput.vue:255-268 only focuses in propose mode). Route the glass half to the glass-ui session.

findings.title: A successful propose leaves the toolbar in propose mode and fills the name field with the CSS color string
findings.owner: CONSUMER demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:233-245 (comment 'Signal parent to exit propose mode' at :239 has no emit; ActionBarLayer.vue never leaves 'propose')

The name field now shows 'lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)', i.e. a color string sitting in the name field. proposedName is '' so the arrow is disabled but still painted in the accent. There is no success confirmation. e2e/smoke/flows/color-propose.spec.ts ('a successful propose returns the toolbar to its actions state') asserts the opposite behaviour.

findings.fix: Add defineEmits(['proposed']) to ColorInput and emit after proposeColorName resolves. ActionBarLayer handles it by setting toolbarMode='actions'. Delete the innerText=formattedCurrentColor write at :240-242 in propose mode. Add a glass toast or aria-live 'Name proposed' confirmation.

findings.title: Invalid-parse feedback is transient and swallowed: pressing Enter again on the same invalid text does nothing, and the error clears after 2 s while the bad text stays
findings.owner: CONSUMER demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:51-64,87 (previousInvalid guard) and :56-60 (2000 ms auto-clear)
findings.frame: 1440-light-06-invalid-enter-400ms.png, 1440-light-06b-invalid-enter-again-same-text.png (log C-enter1+400ms err:true; C-enter1+3.2s err:false with text 'zzzz'; C-enter2-same-text+400ms err:false)
findings.observed: The first Enter on 'zzzz' flashes the error. 2 s later the error clears while 'zzzz' is still in the field. A second Enter on the same text returns silently at the previousInvalid guard, so the user gets no feedback. The debounced path (2 s after typing) re-flashes once, and only for new text.
findings.expected: The invalid state is tied to the field content: it stays while the content is invalid and every submit of invalid content reports it. Glass has the grammar for this: the Input `invalid` prop (input/types.ts), and LabeledField's `invalid` flag plus #error slot (labeled-field/LabeledField.vue:25,59-66).
findings.fix: Replace flashParseError/previousInvalid with a computed `invalid` derived from the last parse of the current text. Clear it only when the text changes to something valid. Bind aria-invalid and the glass invalid state. Keep the one-shot celebrate beat only as decoration on submit.

findings.title: The 'not a valid color' badge covers the typed text and the send button, and spills past the field onto the dock separator

findings.title: The 'live parse' isn't live: a 2 s debounce, and the echo readout only appears in a hover popover that doesn't open while you type

I re-read frames 02, 02p, 03, 04-dock, 05, 06, 06c-dock, 06d, 08, 08a-dock, 11-dock and log rows 4-44 of capture-log-1440-light.jsonl, and re-read ColorInput.vue, ActionBarLayer.vue, useColorParsing.ts, ParseEchoReadout.vue, e2e color-propose.spec.ts, glass Popover.vue, useDockState.ts, the dock README and DESIGN.md. Outcome: 17 findings. 11 CONFIRMED, 5 AMENDED, 1 left PLAUSIBLE (no surviving evidence), 0 REFUTED. The main owner correction: finding 1 is mostly CONSUMER, not GLASS. Glass already ships the hold, and value.js does not use it.

verdicts.title: Opening the color input collapses the dock to the swatch orb and leaves the 'Enter a color' popover floating on its own
verdicts.why: The symptom is CONFIRMED. 02 and 02p show a 56px orb with the popover hanging to its right, and log row 4 has dock 56x56 collapsed:true, pop null at input-open. The owner split is wrong, though: this is mostly CONSUMER. Glass already provides both holds the finding asks glass to add. (1) glass Popover has a `keepDockOpen` prop that takes a dock keepOpen token while the popover is open (src/components/popover/Popover.vue:24,95, via useDockParticipation). It is also in the installed 7.0.0 dist (dist/components/popover/Popover.vue.d.ts:15). (2) useDockState.onMouseLeave returns early while keepOpenCount>0 (useDockState.ts:275-295), and GlassDock binds @focusin/@focusout (GlassDock.vue:349-350). The dock README :67 says the consumer wires overlay open state to keepOpen. ColorInput.vue:3-8 passes no keep-dock-open, and the field is never focused in input mode (the :253-268 watch focuses only when propose is true), so neither hold engages. Consumer fix: add keep-dock-open to the Popover (or take a keepOpen token while toolbarMode !== 'actions') and focus the field on open. The glass half should be narrowed to one PLAUSIBLE question for the glass session: does the dock's own content resize under a stationary pointer fire mouseleave? useDockState.ts:150-154 claims the hit frame never sweeps under the cursor. Do not relay 'add a popover/focus hold' to glass as a defect.

verdicts.title: A successful propose leaves the toolbar in propose mode and fills the name field with the CSS color string
verdicts.why: 11-dock shows 'lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)' in the name field and the ⋮ toggle still showing. Log row 42 has toggles ['Close propose'], send disabled:true opacity 1. Code: ColorInput.vue:238-242 writes innerText = formatCssCaption(...) under the comment 'Signal parent to exit propose mode', and there is no defineEmits. ActionBarLayer only leaves 'propose' via cycleToolbarMode. e2e color-propose.spec.ts:128-168 asserts the opposite, and its own failure message at :167 names the missing signal. The owner is CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: Invalid-parse feedback is transient and swallowed: pressing Enter again on the same invalid text does nothing, and the error clears after 2 s while the bad text stays
verdicts.why: Log rows 18/20/21: err:true at +400ms, err:false at +3.2s with 'zzzz' still in the field, err:false after a second Enter on the same text. Code: useColorParsing.ts:59 (2000 ms auto-clear) and :64 (`input === previousInvalid` early return). The glass invalid grammar exists: the installed 7.0.0 components.css ships aria-invalid:border-(--destructive) and :user-invalid ring utilities. CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: The 'not a valid color' badge covers the typed text and the send button, and spills past the field onto the dock separator
verdicts.why: CONFIRMED by 06: the red chip covers all of 'zzzz', runs past the field's left edge onto the separator, and there is no aria-live (ColorInput.vue:86-90, .error-badge :349-367 with --radius-sm and a raw --destructive fill). Correction: the second citation is wrong. 06d shows 'notacolor(' with NO badge (log row 26: err:false at probeB+3.5s, because the 2 s clear had already fired). Drop 06d as evidence, or replace it with the log row 24 state (err:true at D-typed+2.4s), which has no surviving frame.

verdicts.title: The dock field is a hand-rolled contenteditable span: a square white 4px box inside the stadium dock instead of the glass dock-field or Input pill
verdicts.why: 03, 11-dock and 06 show an opaque white box with 4px corners inside the stadium dock. Log: radius 4px, bg rgb(251,250,248). Code: ColorInput.vue:11-16 has contenteditable plus 'bg-background rounded-input'. The glass pin note checks out. The installed glass 7.0.0 dist/styles/components.css line 1 opens with `:root{... --radius:0.25rem; --radius-lg:0.5rem; --radius-sm:0.25rem ...}` and carries `.rounded-input{border-radius:var(--radius-input)}`. Glass DESIGN.md:385 makes --radius-control the stadium for a field, and :429 REMOVES --radius-input. One line-number fix: the stale '8 px' rounded-input line is demo/DESIGN.md:200, not :201. CONSUMER, with the 7.x :root leak relayed to glass as a repin note.

verdicts.title: The field sizes to its content, so the whole dock resizes on every keystroke and an empty field shrinks to a 50px stub with no placeholder
verdicts.why: 04-dock shows an empty white stub holding only the arrow. Log row 12: input 50px, dock 192px, text '\n', ph null. The width series is confirmed across rows 12/17/23/28 (50→96→165→325px). data-placeholder is set only in propose mode (ColorInput.vue:262), and the text is centred (:16 text-center). CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: The 'live parse' isn't live: a 2 s debounce, and the echo readout only appears in a hover popover that doesn't open while you type
verdicts.why: CONFIRMED: debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000) at useColorParsing.ts:94, and in 05 the field shows oklch(0.7 0.25 150) while the picker still reads Lab 92/88.8/20, with no echo on screen. The fix needs to go further. ParseEchoReadout (ParseEchoReadout.vue:32-35) renders astEcho/gamutVerdict, which derive from model.value.color (useColorParsing.ts:102-104). That is the COMMITTED color, not the field text. So the echo never parses what is being typed. While the text is partial or invalid, it shows the old color's AST and gamut verdict with full confidence, and cutting the debounce to about 200 ms does not change that. The echo should parse the field text: show the candidate AST, or an 'unparsed' state. The duplicated value (03: field + serialized line + echo) is confirmed.

verdicts.title: The hover popover on a text field carries instructions that belong in the placeholder or description, in three typefaces
verdicts.why: 03 and 02p: display-serif title, serif body with italic 'Any', mono value and mono echo, amber verdict. The popover covers the About pane heading in 03 and floats free of the dock in 02/02p. Code: ColorInput.vue:3-8 trigger='hover' open-delay 300, and :94-110. Glass Popover.vue:18-19 documents hover as a 'pointer-adaptive hover preview' (it swaps to a click root on coarse pointers). No suggestions are offered. CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: Mode toggle cycles through three states and each icon shows the next state; ⋮ means 'Close'
verdicts.why: ActionBarLayer.vue:49-80: the icon and label show the destination. In 11-dock and 08, ⋮ = 'Close propose', and 06 shows the Tag icon in input mode. When canProposeName is false, the input-mode glyph is also EllipsisVertical, meaning 'Close input' (:67,77). DockControl does not get `active`. CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: The send arrow has no accessible name and its disabled state looks the same as enabled
verdicts.why: Log rows 4 and 42: send label null, 24x24, and disabled:true with opacity '1' after success. Code: ColorInput.vue:67-82 has no aria-label, and .send-btn at :336-344 uses --radius-sm. One nuance: the claim that btn-interactive's disabled opacity 'is currently overridden' is not shown. No rule in .send-btn sets opacity, so the atom may simply not paint a disabled register in 7.0.0. The fix stands either way. CONSUMER.

findings.title: A failed slug login is silent: the 404/409/429 copy goes to a ref that is never bound

findings.observed: The layer closes about 60ms after Enter and the dock returns to Home/Tools/Login. The server returns 404, which the console logs. No text, toast, role=alert or role=status appears anywhere (capture-log alerts=[]), and the user stays logged out with no explanation.
findings.expected: The authored copy ('Slug not found.', 'Already signed in as this slug.', 'Too many attempts.') appears in the surface the act was taken from, as the identity verdict already does at ProfileSection.vue:100-108.

findings.title: Any string that is not a 4-word slug becomes an admin token: a typo logs you out and turns on admin mode
findings.owner: CONSUMER — SlugEditLayer.vue:25-27,45-46 (`isAdmin = !looksLikeSlug(normalized)`) + useSlugMigration.ts:104-108 (clearUserSlug(), then adminLogin(value), then route to palettes) + demo/platform/auth/useAdminAuth.ts:35-38 (stores the token with no server check)
findings.observed: The 3-word typo is stored as palette-admin-token='brave-quiet-amber'. The user slug is cleared, the route jumps to #/palettes, and the dock turns gold with an 'admin' pill (metrics adminPill=['admin']). A logged-in user who mistypes their slug loses their identity and silently enters an unverified admin mode.
findings.expected: The field classifies input explicitly. A slug-shaped near miss is rejected with inline copy. An admin token is verified by the server (for example a HEAD against an admin endpoint) before the client clears the user identity or claims admin mode.
findings.fix: Split the classification three ways: 4-word slug → login; `ADMIN_TOKEN=` prefix or a verified token → admin; anything else → inline 'Not a slug' error. Verify the token before calling clearUserSlug. Put looksLikeSlug and normalizeTokenInput in one shared module (see the duplicate-twin finding).

findings.title: When regenerate fails, the stored identity is already wiped, while the UI still shows the old slug
findings.owner: CONSUMER — demo/platform/auth/useUserAuth.ts:118-120 (safeRemoveItem(SLUG_KEY) and clearPersistedToken() run BEFORE createSession() at :123; on throw nothing is restored)
findings.where: dock slug-edit layer · Generate new slug (logged in, API unreachable)
findings.observed: After the failure, localStorage palette-user-slug is null and the token is cleared, but the menu still shows 'sable-wishing-charcoal-impala' with 'The new slug was not issued: Backend unreachable — working locally.' A reload silently logs the user out, and the old identity is gone.
findings.expected: Replacing the identity is atomic: the old slug and token are cleared only after the new session is issued, or restored when createSession throws. The verdict's 'working locally' promise is then true.
findings.fix: Snapshot the slug and token, attempt createSession, and persist the new pair on success or restore the snapshot on failure. deleteSession of the old session should come after the new one is issued.

verdicts.title: A failed slug login is silent: the 404/409/429 copy goes to a ref that is never bound
verdicts.why: Confirmed. useSlugMigration.ts:62 declares slugBarRef, :134-137 write to it, and the composable returns it at :175. usePalettePorts.ts:158-168 (sessionPort) does not forward it, and grep finds no binding anywhere in demo. Every error branch is therefore a no-op. SlugEditLayer.vue:54-56 closes the layer without awaiting. The console shows the 404 (1440-light-08 consoleErrors) and the frame shows nothing. Precision fix: capture-log alerts are not literally []; they hold live-region text ('Home view', 'Loading the scene…'). No error copy appears in any role=alert or role=status. The claim that there is 'no port export' should read 'returned by the composable but dropped by usePalettePorts'. Owner CONSUMER is correct.

verdicts.title: The 'switching' spinner can never show: onSlugSwitch is not awaited
verdicts.why: SlugEditLayer.vue:54 calls pm.onSlugSwitch(...) without await. Everything after :42 runs synchronously, and finally (:68-69) resets slugSwitching in the same tick, so Loader2 (:108) never paints. Frames 06/07 at both viewports show spinner=false with loginBtn=true and the layer gone. Awaiting alone is not enough: onSlugSwitch catches internally (:127-138) and never rejects, which is why the fix correctly depends on the outcome being returned. Owner CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: Any string that is not a 4-word slug becomes an admin token: a typo logs you out and turns on admin mode
verdicts.why: SlugEditLayer.vue:46 sets isAdmin = !looksLikeSlug. useSlugMigration.ts:104-108 then runs clearUserSlug and adminLogin and routes to palettes, and useAdminAuth.ts:35-38 stores the token with no server check. Measured: 1440-light-09 and 390-dark-09 have ls palette-admin-token='brave-quiet-amber', adminPill=['admin'], url #/palettes. 'dev' behaves the same (frame 05). Owner CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: When regenerate fails, the stored identity is already wiped, while the UI still shows the old slug
verdicts.why: Confirmed. useUserAuth.ts:118-119 clear SLUG_KEY and the token before createSession (:122). Frames 1440-light-13/14 and 390-light-14 show ls palette-user-slug=null while the menu still shows the old slug with the 'working locally' verdict. Amendment: :113-116 also call deleteSession() on the OLD server session first. Restoring localStorage on failure is therefore not enough, because the old token is already revoked server-side. The fix must reorder the calls (issue the new session, then persist it, then delete the old one), not only snapshot and restore. The docblock at :109-111 ('Atomically replace') is false. Owner CONSUMER.

verdicts.title: 'Generate new slug' failures started from the layer are invisible (always when logged out, until the menu is reopened when logged in)

findings.title: GitHub row: `as-child` is ignored by glass DropdownMenuItem, so the row is a DIV menuitem wrapping an inline <a>. Keyboard Enter and taps on the row padding do nothing, and the icon stacks above the label
findings.owner: CONSUMER demo/shell/dock/menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:111-118 (twin demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue:177); GLASS DropdownMenuItem (glass-ui/src/components/menu/DropdownMenuItem.vue:7-14 has no asChild prop, so the attribute falls through)
findings.where: all themes, 390 menu open (in+out) and the 1440 desktop twin
findings.state: menu open; keyboard focus on GitHub; Enter
findings.observed:
DOM is
…GitHub
. The row is 55px tall where the other rows are 44px, and the icon sits on its own line above 'GitHub'. Enter on the focused row closes the menu and opens no page (pages 1→1). A tap on the row's right padding also opens nothing. Only a tap on the anchor text itself navigates.

findings.title: Slug edit layer (reached from Login / Switch account) overflows the 390 dock: Cancel is fully off-screen, regenerate is clipped, and the placeholder is truncated

findings.title: Glass menu CSS sits outside any cascade layer, so every consumer utility on a menu row is dead: `text-small` and `text-muted-foreground` never apply
findings.owner: GLASS dropdown-menu (dist/glass-ui.css: `.dropdown-menu__item` at offset 29179, outside `@layer components` which spans 2503–19139; the rule sets `color: inherit; font-size: var(--dropdown-text)`). CONSUMER sites that look styled but are not: MobileMenuDropdown.vue:52,55,58,62,90,107,111,120
findings.where: 390 both themes (and every consumer of DropdownMenuItem)
findings.frame: light-390-in-1-open.png (the 'Regenerate slug' row is not muted); probe-measure.mjs output
findings.observed: The 'Regenerate slug' row has class text-muted-foreground but computes to rgb(28,25,23), the same colour as 'Logout'. Every row has class text-small (clamp(.875rem…)) but computes to 21px. The unlayered glass rule beats Tailwind's @layer utilities.
findings.expected: Glass component CSS ships inside `@layer components`, like the rest of glass-ui.css, so consumer utilities and the documented class prop can adjust a row (DESIGN: tokens and class passthrough are the override channel).
findings.fix: GLASS: wrap the dropdown-menu component styles (and the other unlayered component blocks) in @layer components. CONSUMER: once that lands, remove the per-row `text-small` (rows should read the governed --dropdown-text), and keep or drop `text-muted-foreground` on purpose.

verdicts.title: GitHub row: as-child ignored, so the row is a DIV menuitem around an inline <a>; Enter and row-padding taps do nothing; icon stacks
verdicts.why: Reproduced: Enter on the focused GitHub row leaves pages at 1→1; the row is 55px on coarse and 46px on fine pointer where the other rows are 44; the outerHTML is a div[role=menuitem] with an <a> inside; the svg computes display:block, which is why it stacks, and the icon also stacks on fine pointer (c-light-390-in-open-fine.png). The GLASS fix is wrong. Glass removed the polymorphic API on purpose: glass-ui/src/components/_shared/primitive.ts:23 POLYMORPHIC_ATTRS = {as, asChild, as-child} are stripped by fixedHostAttrs ('without reviving a retired polymorphic API'), and DropdownMenuItem.vue:38 hard-codes as="div". Re-adding asChild at glass would reverse a deliberate ruling. Owner: CONSUMER now, with @select → window.open(repo,'_blank','noopener') in both twins. A request for a first-class link item (href prop or DropdownMenuLinkItem) can go to glass as an idea, not as a bug. Severity BROKEN stands.

verdicts.title: Slug edit layer overflows the 390 dock: Cancel off-screen, regenerate clipped, placeholder truncated
verdicts.why: Fresh numbers at ce391643 match exactly: clip [50,340] overflow:auto; input [75,235] (160px = w-40); submit [241,285]; regen [312,356]; cancel [363,407]. c-light-390-in-slug-layer.png and c-dark-390-out-login.png both show 'enter slug or toker', and neither Cancel nor the X glyph is visible. verdicts.title: Glass menu CSS sits outside any cascade layer, so text-small and text-muted-foreground on rows are dead
verdicts.why: The mechanism is confirmed in the live CSSOM: '.dropdown-menu__item, .dropdown-menu__sub-trigger {color:inherit; font-size:var(--dropdown-text)}' is UNLAYERED, while .text-small and .text-muted-foreground sit in @layer utilities (and in components). The Regenerate row computes rgb(28,25,23) at 21px like every other row. The fix is already in glass: glass HEAD CHANGELOG ('Changed — every library style rule sits in @layer components', 466 rules moved and styles.css opening with '@layer theme, base, components, utilities;') covers the post-9.0.0 major. So this is not a new glass bug to relay. The fix is to publish that unreleased major and have the consumer adopt it, 7.0.0 → HEAD. HIGH stands for the consumer's dead classes until then.

verdicts.title: Mobile menu rows render at 21px; the 215px menu reads as a billboard and covers ~half the viewport
verdicts.why: The symptom is confirmed: coarse pointer gives 21px rows and a 215×441 menu (52% of 844). The stated cause is wrong. The installed 7.0.0 dist (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css) already sets --dropdown-text: var(--control-text), the same as glass HEAD sizing.css:62, so no release 'cures' this. The 21px comes from glass light-dark.css:16-20: @media (pointer: coarse) sets --ui-scale to var(--ui-coarse-scale, 1.5), which multiplies type as well as control heights. The probe measured --ui-scale 1.5 on coarse, and on fine pointer at the same 390 viewport the rows are 14px (c-light-390-in-open-fine.png). The 1440 twin is smaller because of the fine pointer, not the width. Owner: GLASS policy. The coarse amplification scales font-size where DESIGN intends touch height to come from padding and the --control-floor. Relay it as an --ui-coarse-scale-on-type issue. Consumer escape hatch: retune --ui-coarse-scale, though a local override is discouraged.

findings.title: A failed 'Regenerate slug' signs the user out but the menu keeps showing the old identity
findings.owner: CONSUMER demo/platform/auth/useUserAuth.ts:112-126 (regenerate) + demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:87-100
findings.state: profile menu open, identity verdict = failed
findings.where: ProfileSection.vue:96-108 (verdict render); root cause in useUserAuth.regenerate
findings.observed: With POST /sessions returning 503, the verdict reads 'The new slug was not issued: Service Unavailable'. The header pill still shows the old slug (woven-nesting-pearl-toad / smoky-dipping-citrine-stork) and the dock still says 'Profile'. But regenerate() already DELETEd the session and removed palette-user-slug and the token from storage: localStorage slug = null, and the console shows a 401. After a reload the dock shows 'Login', so the user was signed out and the verdict never said so.
findings.expected: A failed identity act leaves the prior identity intact, or the UI and the verdict truthfully report the sign-out. The CARRY LOCK comment at ProfileSection.vue:96-99 promises that the act's outcome is what gets rendered.
findings.fix: Issue the new session first and revoke the old one only after success. On failure keep the old slug and token persisted. If revoking first is unavoidable, clear the slug ref on failure and say 'You were signed out; the new slug was not issued'.

findings.title: Signing in with an unknown slug fails silently: the error goes to an unmounted PaletteSlugBar
findings.owner: CONSUMER demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:117-128 + demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:53-55

verdicts.title: GitHub row: as-child dropped, icon stacks above label, only text navigates

verdicts.title: 'Share color' copies a URL without the color
verdicts.why: All four clipboard readbacks are exactly 'http://localhost:9000/#/'. App.vue:529-530 copies window.location.href. useColorUrl.ts writes the query only from the debounced Model→URL watch, which is gated on `live`, so a boot color restored from storage never reaches the address. The fix of serializing from the model is sound.

verdicts.title: Desktop @mbabb trigger is a ghost Button, not the dock dropdown trigger
verdicts.why: The defect holds. 1440-light-0b-closed-dock-zoom shows a muddy gray capsule next to the flat Home and Tools. triggerCls includes 'glass-wash glass-capsule glass-capsule-hover … hover:underline', and the trigger computes underline in the open probe. Two corrections. (1) The canon cited is stale: glass HEAD retired DockDropdownTrigger into DockTrigger for="dropdown" (dock/index.ts:26, DockTrigger.vue:15-23), so DESIGN.md:1047 is doc drift that should go to glass. (2) DockTrigger renders its built-in ChevronDown only for for="select" (DockTrigger.vue:54-62), so moving to for="dropdown" does not give a chevron. The consumer has to add one, or glass has to add it to the dropdown leg. The Login button beside it has the same gray capsule (see missed).

verdicts.title: Menu typography split three ways; text-small overrides tokens; font-display dead
verdicts.why: The open probe computes the menu content in Fira Code, the headerLink in Fira Code 16.4px, the headerTag in Fraunces italic 11px, and every row in Plus Jakarta Sans 16.4px. Glass semantic.css:217-219 `text-small` sets font-family var(--font-text), which beats the foundation.css:420 --dropdown-menu-font mono token. The owner call (consumer) is correct.

verdicts.title: Dark mode row: static label, no checked state, mis-sized icon
verdicts.why: The probe shows icons [[14,14],[14,14],[16,24]], and the source is `aspect-square w-4` with no height (ProfileSection.vue:193-194). 1440-light-2b-open-zoom shows a Sun beside 'Dark mode'. The row is a plain DropdownMenuItem with no aria-checked, and glass ships DropdownMenuCheckboxItem. Rider: glass already banked the related inbound O-61 ('DarkModeToggle has no menu-item form', glass commit fe5df357), so any glass half of this is already routed. Cross-reference it instead of opening a duplicate.

verdicts.title: Header repeats trigger label, second GitHub link, outside keyboard roving
verdicts.why: In the source the header is a bare <a href=github.com/mkbabb> in a div (ProfileSection.vue:163-171), and the row goes to github.com/mkbabb/value.js. 1440-dark-4-kbd-focus shows ArrowDown roving Share→GitHub with the header never highlighted. The avatar also probes at borderRadius 0px on its host.

verdicts.title: @mbabb block hand-duplicated across desktop and mobile twins
verdicts.why: ProfileSection.vue:163-196 and MobileMenuDropdown.vue:94-133 are byte-identical in the avatar/header, Share, as-child GitHub with the inline SVG path, and the Dark mode rows, including the w-4 icon and text-small.

verdicts.title: Hover and keyboard highlight light two rows; light hover wash nearly invisible
verdicts.why: 1440-dark-4-kbd-focus shows Share still washed while GitHub carries the highlight ring. 1440-light-3-hover-share shows the hovered Share row barely distinct from rest. At glass HEAD, menu.css paints `.glass-menu-row:hover` (in @media (hover:hover)) and `[data-highlighted]` as independent legs with the same --menu-row-bg, so a pointer resting on one row while the keyboard moves on paints both. This is still true at HEAD, and GLASS is the right owner. One nuance for the fix: the :hover leg also carries the pointer-only lift, so glass should keep the lift but gate the fill on [data-highlighted].

verdicts.title: DropdownMenuContent corner 12px (panel rung), not card, outside overlay-plate
verdicts.why: The observation is correct for what ships. menuCls is 'dropdown-menu-content dropdown-menu__content glass-reveal glass-floating', and the 7.0.0 glass-ui.css has `.dropdown-menu__content{…border-radius:var(--radius-panel)}`, which is 12px. But glass HEAD has already cured it: DropdownMenuContent.vue now takes overlayContentAttrs (_shared/overlay/content.ts:57-60), which writes 'glass-overlay-plate glass-reveal', so --radius-ctx is var(--radius-card) at 16px (overlay-plate.css:63). The owner is therefore CONSUMER/pin (value.js pins ^7.0.0 and resolves 7.0.0), and the glass session has nothing new to fix. Route it as 'adopt the glass release that carries the overlay-plate menu' plus a verify-after-bump, not as a fresh glass defect.

confirm.page: value.js palettes-view (/#/palettes), fresh confirm seat. I re-read the frames under docs/tranches/X/audit/ui-evidence/value/palettes-view/ (loaded/searchnone/selected/menucolor/offline/rename/dupe at 1440, plus selected and loaded at 390) and checked the source claims. Trees at confirm time: value.js ace3a5d7 with 6 dirty files, glass-ui 6433284a with 3 dirty files. Both moved since the audit, but every cited consumer line still matches. The installed @mkbabb/glass-ui is 7.0.0. Result: 17 CONFIRMED and 5 AMENDED, 0 REFUTED. Three owner calls are wrong. (a) The menu mono comes from the CONSUMER: demo/styles/foundation.css:419 sets `--dropdown-menu-font: var(--font-mono)`, and glass root deliberately retired the `--dropdown-menu-{font,...}` knobs (glass src/components/_shared/menu/menu.css:125). Asking glass for a new menu font token would recreate a knob glass has already ruled out. (b, c) The two SearchBar asks go to a component that no longer exists: glass deleted SearchBar with its ./search subpath (src/components/input/index.ts:6, BK #42). The fix is to move the consumer onto glass Input, and the seated-register ask goes on Input only. The WatercolorDot findings get worse on inspection. The 7.0.0 dist (watercolor-dot.js:79-110) sets inheritAttrs:false, renders a fixed `<span aria-hidden>` with an inline `pointer-events:none`, and has no slot. So the add slot's Plus glyph never renders (the frames show an empty dashed blob), and the touch Popover path (PopoverTrigger as-child) is dead too, not only the hover path. The pane's radius holds up: single-line controls are stadiums and holders are 16px, which is canon.

In the dist (watercolor-dot.js:79-110) the span also carries an inline pointerEvents:'none' and has no renderSlot, so the <Plus> child (CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:104) is dropped. The add slot shows as an empty dashed blob with no '+' in every frame (loaded__1440__light.png, searchnone__1440__dark.png). audit.page: value.js palette-scene-actions: the selected palette's verbs in the dock. Reached from /#/palettes (a saved local palette offers Rename, Publish, Export, Delete) and from /#/browse (an owned remote palette offers Save, Rename, Tags, Versions, Make private, Remix, Vote, Export, Delete). Captured at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark, in headed Chromium on the served dev page http://localhost:9000/. The API was routed only at the page's network boundary: 'down' means connection refused; 'up' means a mocked owned palette whose mutations return 500. Deselecting works: the dock goes back to the 'Tools' colour set (frames *-09-deselected-label and *-09b-deselected-tools-set; probe-two-log.json afterDeselectSecond='Tools'). Only one palette can be selected across the two panes (probe-two-selected-1440.png, selectedCards=1).
audit.frames: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/X/audit/ui-evidence/value/palette-scene-actions/ holds 116 PNGs: {light,dark}-{1440,390}-01..18 per state, plus probe-*, sheet-* and crop-*. MANIFEST.txt records the tree HEAD and dirty count beside each capture set. HEAD moved while I was capturing because other workflows committed: light-1440 at e97c8afc (dirty 22); dark-1440, light-390, dark-390 and probe at f95a2f77 (dirty 4, 5, 20, 20); probe-two at 5ac82779 (dirty 5). The raw per-step data is in capture-log-*.json, probe-log.json and probe-two-log.json. The scripts are capture.mjs, probe.mjs and probe-two.mjs. I only read and captured; nothing outside the audit folder was changed.

findings.title: Edit tags opens the tag editor unanchored at the viewport's top-left corner
findings.state: owned remote palette selected -> dock 'Edit tags' (the card menu uses the same popover)
findings.observed: The TAGS popover renders at box {x:0,y:4,w:208} (capture-log-*.json step 14). At 390 it covers the dock and the seat's hover card. It is not attached to the card or to the seat that opened it.
findings.expected: A glass Popover is anchored to its trigger or anchor (glass-ui src/components/popover). The editor should open on the selected palette, or on the seat that dispatched it.
findings.owner: CONSUMER
findings.where: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:152-159 mounts <TagEditPopover> with no #trigger slot. demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:2-6 has PopoverTrigger around an empty slot.
findings.fix: Give TagEditPopover a PopoverAnchor bound to the selected card's element, or to the dispatching dock seat. Alternatively, make it a placed Dialog. Never mount PopoverContent without an anchor.

findings.title: Dock 'Delete palette' destroys a saved palette instantly: no confirm, no undo, no message
findings.observed: One click removes 'Moss & Slate' with no dialog, alertdialog or message (step 10: dialog 0, alertdialog 0, remaining 1). The dock silently falls back to the colour Tools set, and an unprompted 'Extract palette' hover card appears.
findings.expected: The app's own destructive policy: deleting an owned palette in Browse asks for confirmation (BrowsePane.vue:196), and 'Delete all' asks too (PalettesPane.vue:122-140). The same verb from the same dock needs the same guard.
findings.owner: CONSUMER
findings.fix: Route local delete through the same confirm Dialog Browse uses, or delete with an undo toast. Use one destructive-verb policy for both panes and for the dock.

findings.title: At 390 the 9-verb palette set overflows the dock: Remix clipped mid-icon, Vote/Export/Delete off-screen
findings.observed: The dock is 312px wide. The layer's content is 421px wide in a 290px client area, with overflow-x:auto (probe-log.json). Save, Rename, Tags, Versions and Private are visible. Remix is cut through its icon. Vote, Export and Delete are only reachable by a horizontal swipe that nothing on screen suggests.
findings.expected: Per the glass dock README (:50-52), capped runs fall back to native scrolling only. The consumer should not overflow a phone dock with a flat list of 9 verbs, and a destructive verb should never be hidden off-canvas.
findings.owner: CONSUMER
findings.where: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:930-995 (paletteActions emits every offered verb as a flat seat row)
findings.fix: Rank the verbs. Keep 3-4 primary seats (for example Rename, Export, Vote/Save) and put the rest behind one DockTrigger overflow menu that reuses PaletteCardMenu's item list. Or cap the seat count by viewport.

findings.title: Palette seats are hand-rolled buttons, not DockControl: 32px, 4px radius, below the 44px touch floor
findings.state: any palette verb set, both widths
findings.observed: The seats are <button class='action-button-wrapper ... rounded-sm'>, 32x32 with a 4px radius, even with touch emulated at 390. The Back control in the same row is DockControl ('dock-icon-button glass-specular-track glass-capsule-hover'): 40x40 on desktop, 46.8x46.8 on touch, stadium radius. So one row has two different button faces.
findings.expected: The glass dock README says 'DockControl is the button face' and that interactive controls keep a 44px coarse-pointer target floor. DESIGN.md: --radius-control is a stadium for a single-line control.
findings.owner: CONSUMER
findings.fix: Render each seat as <DockControl shape="icon" :active> and drop the local button face. The hover hint then becomes a glass Tooltip on the DockControl.

findings.title: A second verdict within 2.5s is dismissed early by the first verdict's timer
findings.state: two verbs in a row (Vote, then Make private, or Remix then Save)
findings.observed: Measured: 'Vote failed' appears at 168ms. Visibility is clicked at 1110ms and 'Unpublish failed' appears at 1268ms, but it is gone at 2971ms, killed by the vote's timer (168+2500). In the 390 captures the verdicts for steps 13 and 17 never appear in their frames at all.
findings.expected: Every verdict is readable for its full time. W7-mutation-ownership says a failure is rendered where the act was taken.
findings.owner: CONSUMER
findings.where: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue:39-47 (the watch only follows props.visible, so a new message while visible does not restart the timer)
findings.fix: Restart the timer on every showFeedback, by watching [message, visible] or taking a nonce. Do not auto-dismiss error verdicts.

findings.title: Result of a dock verb lands only on the card rail: off-screen on phones, gone in 2.5s, and the dock's 'failed' state can never fire
findings.state: publish with the API down; any failed verb dispatched from the dock
findings.frame: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/X/audit/ui-evidence/value/palette-scene-actions/light-1440-06a-publish-1s.png (visible at 1.2s) vs light-1440-06-publish-failed-api-down.png (gone by 6s); sheet-light-390-a.png frame 4 and sheet-dark-390-a.png frame 2 (the failure is below the fold, never seen)
findings.observed: 'Failed to publish: Backend unreachable' shows on the card for 2.5s and then disappears. At 390 the user is looking at the dock at the top of the page while the card is below the fold. The dock seat stays 'ready', with no destructive colour and no role=alert.
findings.expected: GenericActionBar models a 'failed' state (destructive colour + role=alert, recoverable). An error should persist where the act was taken, which here is the dock.
findings.owner: CONSUMER
findings.where: demo/palettes/PaletteInspector.vue:345-368 (every command is a fire-and-forget emit that never throws or returns a promise) + demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:936-940 (resolve() can only mark failed on a throw) + ActionFeedback.vue:32 (autoDismissMs 2500 for errors too)
findings.fix: Have the host return each mutation's promise through the command, so a rejection lands in the router's failures map and the seat shows 'failed'. Keep error verdicts until dismissed, or use a glass toast that is visible at any scroll position.

verdicts.title: Keyboard focus is invisible on both dialog actions (Cancel and Delete all)
verdicts.why: The symptom is confirmed. p2-light-focus-delete.png and p2-dark-focus-cancel.png show no ring. probe3 dialogBtn has fv:true with bs equal to the resting 0 2px 8px/0.06. Cancel has bs:none. Correction 1: 'Delete all' is data-emphasis=secondary with tone=destructive, not a text arm. The cited HEAD styles.css:177-183 is not the code that runs. In v7.0.0, base.css:113-116 `.focus-ring:focus-visible{box-shadow:var(--focus-ring-shadow)}` loses to v7 button/styles.css:53-56 and :103-106 (box-shadow:none), and to the capsule's resting shadow. Correction 2: the proposed fix is stale. Glass v8.0.0 (70dc0f06, BK #80) moved .focus-ring to an OUTLINE (HEAD utilities/base.css:135-150), and a button's box-shadow cannot hide an outline. So this is a GLASS defect in 7.0.0 that is already fixed at the producer; the consumer owes the adoption (value pins ^7.0.0). New GLASS item to route: DESIGN.md:603 and :611 still describe the retired box-shadow ring, so the canon doc is behind its own stylesheet. Severity stays HIGH.

verdicts.title: Dock collapsed to its blob while the dialog was open
verdicts.why: The observation is confirmed: 1440-light-2-open.png shows the dock as a blob, and 1440-light-0-pane.png shows it expanded. The 'cause unconfirmed' and 'maybe 5s idle' parts can now be settled. Glass v7 useDockState.ts:352-362 `onPointerDownOutside` calls collapse() on any capture-phase pointerdown outside the dock (state machine :76 'PINNED --(clickOutside)--> COLLAPSED'). The pointer click on the trash trigger is that outside pointerdown. The dialog is not involved, and the collapse comes within about 0.7s, well before the 5000ms delay at Dock.vue:161. The probe3 control never clicked the page, which is why it stayed expanded. The probe2 'dockOpen w 1408' numbers measure the .dock-band wrapper and prove nothing either way. Owner: GLASS useDockState click-away policy (a desktop dock that the consumer starts expanded via start-collapsed=false collapses on any content click), plus CONSUMER Dock.vue:159-163 configuration. The same happens for every content click, so it is not specific to this dialog.

findings.title: The tag popover has no anchor: it opens pinned to the viewport's top-left corner from every reach
findings.owner: CONSUMER demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:152-158 (TagEditPopover is rendered with no #trigger slot) + demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:3-5 (PopoverTrigger as-child wraps an empty slot); GLASS popover (src/components/popover/index.ts exports no PopoverAnchor; PopoverTrigger.vue:25 strips `reference`), so a popover opened from code cannot be anchored
findings.where: /#/browse, open state, all 4 viewport/theme combinations, reached from the card menu and from the dock
findings.observed: The dialog box measures x=0, y=4, w=208 in every capture, far from the card or dock button that opened it. At 390 it covers the dock's search and kebab controls and the Browse scene title.
findings.expected: A floating surface sits next to the control that opened it (glass popover placement: side/align/sideOffset, avoidCollisions). A menu-item or dock-verb reach should anchor to the card's menu trigger or the inspector.
findings.fix: GLASS: export a PopoverAnchor, or accept a `reference` (virtual element) on Popover/PopoverContent instead of stripping it. CONSUMER: anchor to the card's ... trigger or the inspector element. At 390, present the editor in the glass Sheet (bottom) instead of a floating popover.

findings.title: A failed tag save leaves the unsaved tag shown as applied: the card count stays and the checkbox stays checked
findings.owner: CONSUMER demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:76-77 (emits update:tags BEFORE saveTags and ignores its result) + demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:423-431 (onTagsUpdated writes the tags into remotePalettes unconditionally)
findings.observed: PATCH {tags:[cool,pastel]} returned 500. 'pastel' stays checked in the popover and the card goes from +1 to +2. The error ('The tags were not saved: Server exploded') appears only as a card rail verdict, away from the act; after close it is gone and the card still shows +2.
findings.expected: The failure is shown where the user acted (W7 failure-dispositions row 3) and the displayed state matches the server: the change is rolled back or marked unsaved.
findings.fix: Emit update:tags only after saveTags resolves with a palette, or restore the previous tags when it returns undefined. Render tagEdit.error inside the popover as role=alert under the list.

findings.title: An unreachable tag catalog is shown as 'No tags available.' and nothing reports the failure
findings.owner: CONSUMER demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:16-18 (empty and error share one branch; tagEdit.error is never read) + demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:452-458 (the verdict watch skips while tagEditPalette is null at mount, and does not fire again when the next failure has the same message)

findings.fix: Add a `v-else-if="tagEdit.error.value"` branch with the message and a Retry button that calls loadAllTags(true); keep 'No tags available.' for a true empty catalog.

findings.title: Each click sends its own PATCH, with no pending state and the saved palette thrown away
findings.owner: CONSUMER demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:64-78 (the saveTags return value is discarded; nothing marks a row pending) + demo/palettes/useTagEdit.ts:65-89
findings.frame: 1440-light-04-tag-added.png, 1440-light-05-tag-removed.png; PATCH bodies and If-Match in log-1440-light.json rec.patches

verdicts.title: The tag popover has no anchor: it opens pinned to the viewport's top-left corner from every reach

The logs record box x=0 y=4 w=208 at every viewport. At 390 it covers the Browse title and the search kebab. The GLASS half is also confirmed. glass src/components/popover/index.ts exports only Popover, PopoverTrigger and PopoverContent (no PopoverAnchor, no match anywhere in glass src), and PopoverTrigger.vue:25 strips `reference`. So a consumer cannot anchor a popover it opens from code. verdicts.why: In 390-dark-09, pastel is checked, the card shows +2, and the red rail verdict sits on the card, not in the popover. In 1440-light-10, after close the card still reads +2 and the verdict is gone. Log patches[2] is {tags:[cool,pastel]} in fail mode. verdicts.title: An unreachable tag catalog is shown as 'No tags available.' and nothing reports the failure
verdicts.why: The popover content is identical in 12 and 13 ('TAGS / No tags available.', both 122.97px high), but the frames are not pixel-identical: the md5 hashes differ at all four viewports. Frame 1440-light-12 has a global top-right pill, 'BACKEND OFFLINE — SAVED LOCALLY', which the log's alerts list confirms. So one failure signal exists, but it is generic, sits far from the act, and is wrong. The backend is not offline (only GET /tags was refused), and 'saved locally' does not apply to a catalog read. It also offers no retry. The core claim stands: TagEditPopover.vue:16-18 collapses error into empty, and tagEdit.error is never read in the popover. Revised text: 'the only signal is a misleading app-wide backend-offline pill; the popover itself shows the empty state'. Severity stays HIGH, owner CONSUMER.
